description: #3347 — READ-command differential over `run_advanced_query` plus the two agenda list queries. The op sequence only stamps reserved columns on SEED blocks (no create_block), so every queried id is byte-identical on both stacks and the projected rows stay comparable. The State step is the exclude+is_null AND-join (#2019 / #3314 finding 1): the backend emits `todo_state IS NOT NULL AND todo_state NOT IN ('DONE')`, so a mock that OR-joins the two branches matches EVERY row. The DueDate step straddles both Between endpoints (S2 sits on `from`, S4 on `to`): SQL BETWEEN is inclusive, so a half-open mock evaluator drops S4. Neither semantic is reachable through the Pages surface — `PAGES_ALLOWED_KEYS` rejects `state` / `due-date` — which is why `conformance/pages-metadata/filters.vectors.json` cannot cover them and this fixture is their only cross-impl gate.
name: query_advanced_filters

queries.comment: Vacuity guard: a filterless advanced query must return the WHOLE seeded space on both stacks. If this step ever goes empty, the steps below agree only because neither reached any data. NOT `ordered` only because of #3821 (mock sorts `b.id ASC`, engine `b.id DESC`) — every id here is a SEED id, identical on both stacks, so this step can and should pin the order once #3821 lands. `ordered` since #3821 closed (#3927): the engine's terminal tiebreaker is `b.id DESC` and the mock's `resolveSortTerms` now mirrors it, so this sequence pins `run_advanced_query`'s DEFAULT sort arm. An unordered step credits that arm while comparing sets, which is no evidence about an ORDERING branch at all.
queries.name: advanced_no_filter_returns_the_space

queries.comment: #3314 finding 1 (State half): exclude + is_null is an AND-join — non-NULL todo_state that is not DONE. An OR-join is a tautology and returns every row. `ordered` since #3821 closed (#3927): the engine's terminal tiebreaker is `b.id DESC` and the mock's `resolveSortTerms` now mirrors it, so this sequence pins `run_advanced_query`'s DEFAULT sort arm. An unordered step credits that arm while comparing sets, which is no evidence about an ORDERING branch at all.
queries.name: advanced_state_exclude_done_and_unset

queries.comment: #3314 finding 1 (Between half): SQL BETWEEN is inclusive on BOTH endpoints. S2 sits on `from`, S4 on `to`. `ordered` since #3821 closed (#3927): the engine's terminal tiebreaker is `b.id DESC` and the mock's `resolveSortTerms` now mirrors it, so this sequence pins `run_advanced_query`'s DEFAULT sort arm. An unordered step credits that arm while comparing sets, which is no evidence about an ORDERING branch at all.
queries.name: advanced_due_date_between_is_inclusive

queries.comment: S5 is the only task with a todo_state and neither date.
queries.name: agenda_undated_tasks

queries.comment: #3893 — the first fixture step that PAGINATES `run_advanced_query`, and the reason the gap was invisible: the engine's `QueryCursor` had no conformance coverage of any kind, byte or row, so #3863's cursor divergence could not have reddened here no matter what the projection recorded. An EXPLICIT `position` sort, not the default: the default keyset is the bare `b.id` tiebreak, which #3821 (mock `b.id ASC`, engine `b.id DESC`) still orders the other way round, so a default-sorted page pair would redden on a known open bug instead of on this one. `position` is distinct across the seed except for the B1/B2 tie at 1, which is what exercises the appended `b.id DESC` tiebreak. The recorded `cursor` is the TWO-element tagged tuple `[Int,Text]` — the arity is the #3863 class exactly, since the pre-fix mock encoded the id alone.
queries.name: advanced_position_page_1

queries.comment: The resumed page. Its rows are what a wrong boundary VALUE changes, which is why the `cursor` field erases values and pins structure only — the two assertions are complementary, not redundant. This step also needed `cursor_path` fixing: `AdvancedQueryRequest.cursor` is a field of the request DTO, and the harness was injecting a top-level `args.cursor` that the command would have ignored, so a 'second page' step would silently have re-read the FIRST page.
queries.name: advanced_position_page_2

queries.comment: The short final page: one row, `has_more` false, and therefore `cursor` NULL. Pins that the end-of-results signal is not conflated with a full page, and that a last page hands back no cursor to chase.
queries.name: advanced_position_page_3
